# Continuous integration

[`workflows/ci.yml`](workflows/ci.yml) runs on pushes to `main` and pull requests
targeting `main`. Backend and frontend jobs run independently on Ubuntu 24.04;
neither waits for the other. A newer run cancels an obsolete run for the same PR
or branch. This phase builds and tests; it does not deploy, publish containers or
apply migrations to any development/production database.

## Backend

- Installs .NET SDK `10.0.x`. A runner-only `backend/global.json` selects the SDK
  returned by setup-dotnet, even if the runner has a newer SDK preinstalled.
- Caches `~/.nuget/packages` by OS and the two relevant csproj files. The setup
  action's built-in NuGet cache is not enabled because this repository currently
  has no NuGet lockfile. Restore still runs after a cache hit.
- Restores/builds `backend/TenantFlow.slnx`, which references the correct outer API
  and `backend/TenantFlow.Api.Tests`. Build runs once in Release with `--no-restore`.
- Checks Docker and runs the existing integration project with `--no-build` and
  `--no-restore`. Testcontainers starts PostgreSQL with generated credentials,
  creates a database per test and cleans up resources. There is no redundant
  PostgreSQL service, development Compose startup or supplied connection string.
- Uploads available TRX results as `backend-test-results` even after test failure;
  artifacts expire after seven days. No test output is promoted to a deployment.

## Frontend

Installs Node.js 24, which satisfies the installed Vite requirement
(`^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`). setup-node caches npm's download cache using
`frontend/package-lock.json`; it does not cache node_modules. The job runs the
actual configured commands: `npm ci`, `npm run build`, and
`npm run test -- --run` (the existing test script is `vitest run`).

## Permissions and secrets

No repository secrets are required. Dependencies and container images are public;
test passwords and JWT keys are generated by the existing fixture. The host runs
in Testing mode and the fixture clears application/development configuration,
checks its private signing key and verifies database ownership before migrations
and cleanup. Do not add development/production connection strings or JWT keys to
the workflow. No .env file is created or required by CI.

`GITHUB_TOKEN` is supplied automatically by GitHub with only `contents: read`.
Checkout does not persist credentials. Actions are pinned to verified full commit
SHAs; update them through reviewed changes when adopting newer releases. The
workflow uses `pull_request`, never the privileged `pull_request_target` event.

## Local verification and GitHub results

From the repository root, with Docker's Linux engine running:

```powershell
dotnet restore backend/TenantFlow.slnx
dotnet build backend/TenantFlow.slnx --configuration Release --no-restore -p:UseAppHost=false
dotnet test backend/TenantFlow.Api.Tests/TenantFlow.Api.Tests.csproj --configuration Release --no-build --no-restore
cd frontend
npm ci
npm run build
npm run test -- --run
```

On Windows, Docker's credential helper must be on PATH; see the
[integration-test guide](../backend/TenantFlow.Api.Tests/README.md). Local passing
commands and workflow validation do not prove that GitHub CI has passed.

Commit the workflow and this guide, then push your current branch:

```powershell
git add .github/workflows/ci.yml .github/README.md
git commit -m "Add backend and frontend GitHub Actions CI"
git push -u origin HEAD
```

Open a pull request targeting `main`. A push to a feature branch alone does not
trigger this workflow. Open the PR's **Checks** tab, or the repository's
**Actions → CI** page, and inspect both job logs. The run's Artifacts section
contains TRX results when produced. After merge, a push event also validates
`main`. A fork PR may require a maintainer to approve its first run under the
repository's existing Actions policy; no secrets need to be supplied.

Sources: [setup-dotnet](https://github.com/actions/setup-dotnet),
[setup-node caching](https://github.com/actions/setup-node#caching-global-packages-data),
[Testcontainers on GitHub Actions](https://dotnet.testcontainers.org/cicd/).
